title: Chicago, summer 1835

lighting.note: Early afternoon, 1 July 1835. Sun azimuth and elevation are computed from this time and the datum lat/lon and drive both sky and the single directional light. Chosen so the south elevation is genuinely lit — at this latitude in July the sun is high, so vertical surfaces take light at a grazing angle and a mid-morning sun leaves a south wall too dark to read its documented white paint.

anchors.label: The log wing, from the north-west
Lake and Market, the corner itself
Hogan's store, where the mail came
Green Tree Tavern, Lake and Canal
South Water Street, from the Wells Street corner

note: The first scene. Population roughly 3,265 in the late-1835 count; the town is twenty months old and has grown roughly tenfold in two years. Wabansia and Kinzie's Addition are platted (the Wooley correction was approved 17 June 1835, two weeks before this date) but almost entirely unbuilt. Anchor coordinates are provisional until the datum is verified — they are placeholders in the same local frame, not survey positions. Spawn and the near anchors are now derived from the Sauganash's real placement at Lake and Market — about 100 m east and 130 m south of the forks confluence — rather than from the datum origin, which is in the middle of the river. Both anchors that once pointed at a surveyed corner because their records had not landed have now resolved onto it: Green Tree stands at Lake and Canal looking east at the tavern, and South Water stands in the street at Wells. The South Water anchor was moved there on 2026-08-15 from (260, -95), which was 101 m south of the centreline of the street it is named for and framed a field. Its easting is the Wells corner the South Water records are themselves offset from (OpenStreetMap E 447402.5, N 4637411.6, the West Upper Wacker Drive / North Wells junction, quoted in those records' position notes); its northing is the committed South Water centreline at that easting (data/streets/1835.json), which sits about 9 m south of the modern junction centre because the 1835 line is shifted into the dry half of the platted riverfront corridor. A camera is not a placement, and this one claims nothing about a building. The forks anchor moved from (-20, -30) to (-100, -28) once the river channel was traced: the placeholder stood in the middle of the South Branch. It is now on the west bank at Wolf Point, which is what the name meant, looking east across the confluence and down the main stem.
